sheetTitle: Challenges in Teaching –Analog Shortcuts in a Digital World
youtubeTitle: Challenges in Teaching – Analog Shots Solution in a Digital World
author: IIM Bangalore
description: In this video, Prof. Kamath reveals that the issue facing teachers today is something deeper than information being gained through the internet or smartphone – it is around attention spans, concentration levels and an ability to slow down and reflect. She speaks about her “analog shots in a digital world” to address these challenges.

sheetTitle: On Teaching Pedagogies – Case Study Method and Other Methods
youtubeTitle: On Teaching Pedagogies – Case Study Method and Other Methods
author: IIM Bangalore
description: In this short video, Prof. Kamath presents her take on teaching pedagogies: case methods, non-case methods, flipped classrooms, and hybrid classes.

youtubeTitle: Being a Good Teacher
author: IIM Bangalore
description: In this brief video, Prof. Kamath explains why being a good teacher is the same as being a good doctor or a good lawyer.

sheetTitle: When the Teacher Does Not Know the Answer
youtubeTitle: When the Teacher Does Not Know the Answer
author: IIM Bangalore
description: In this brief video, Prof. U Dinesh Kumar speaks from his experience and tells educators what to do when they do not have the answer to a student’s question.

sheetTitle: Desirable Level of Difficulty: Introduction – The 3 Principles
youtubeTitle: Desirable Level of Difficulty: Introduction - The 3 Principles
author: IIM Bangalore
description: In this video, Professor Sourav Mukherji introduces educators to the 3 principles of the Desirable Level of Difficulty – (i) the Generation Effect or Allowing Struggles in Learning for more effective learning; (ii) Spacing to enable better retention; and (iii) Interleaving for the understanding of concepts. He will be covering each of these principles in the Desirable Level of Difficulty series.

sheetTitle: Desirable Level of Difficulty: The Generation Effect or Allowing Struggles in Learning
youtubeTitle: Desirable Level of Difficulty: The Generation Effect or Allowing Struggles in Learning
author: IIM Bangalore
description: This short video is about the first principle in the Desirable Level of Difficulty video series - The Generation Effect or Allowing Struggles in Learning. Professor Sourav Mukherji talks about how learning becomes sustainable in the long run if struggles are allowed in the learning process.

sheetTitle: Desirable Level of Difficulty: Repetition in Learning
youtubeTitle: Desirable Level of Difficulty: Repetition in Learning
author: IIM Bangalore
description: This informative video is about the second principle in the Desirable Level of Difficulty video series - Repetition in Learning. Professor Sourav Mukherji stresses on the known fact that when we repeat something, we learn better.

youtubeTitle: Desirable Level of Difficulty: Interleaving
author: IIM Bangalore
description: In this brief video, Professor Sourav Mukherji talks about the third principle in the Desirable Level of Difficulty video series – Interleaving. This can be a better approach for understanding of concepts.

youtubeTitle: Desirable Level of Difficulty: Conclusion
author: IIM Bangalore
description: In the concluding video of the Desirable Level of Difficulty series, Professor Sourav Mukherji wraps up this series by reiterating that teachers need to be facilitators of learning, but offering too much help to students is not good for the learning process, and this must be kept in mind.

sheetTitle: Preparing for a Class in 4 Steps
youtubeTitle: Preparing for a Class in 4 Steps
author: IIM Bangalore
description: In this video, Prof. Vasanthi Srinivasan brings her 20 years of teaching experience talking about preparing to teach a class. This video will be informative to educators who feel they have not prepared sufficiently for a class or aren’t sure about how much preparation can be labelled sufficient preparation.

youtubeTitle: Session Plan – Development and Process
author: IIM Bangalore
description: In this video, Prof. Vasanthi Srinivasan talks from her experience when she provides tips on developing a session plan and also discusses the process.

youtubeTitle: Creating Energy in the Classroom
author: IIM Bangalore
description: In this brief video, Prof. Vasanthi Srinivasan stresses that as a teacher you need to be enthusiastic in the classroom first, if you want to evoke enthusiasm in your students. She provides helpful tips to create a positive experience in the classroom.

sheetTitle: Creating More Student Engagement in Class
youtubeTitle: Creating More Student Engagement in Class
author: IIM Bangalore
description: In this short video, Prof. Prateek Raj shares his experience in student engagement. He says inclusivity is key and offers tips on creating student engagement.

sheetTitle: Being More Confident in the Classroom
youtubeTitle: Being More Confident in the Classroom
author: IIM Bangalore
description: In this brief video, Prof. Prateek Raj talks about the importance of being well prepared for teachers to be confident in class.

sheetTitle: Teaching Business Management vs. Teaching a Science Course
youtubeTitle: Teaching Business Management vs. Teaching a Science Course by Professor B Mahadevan
author: IIM Bangalore
description: In this video, Prof. B Mahadevan clarifies how teaching in a business school is different from teaching in a science course; a question that many educators think about.

sheetTitle: Tips on Becoming a Great Academic
youtubeTitle: Tips on Becoming a Great Academic by Professor B Mahadevan
author: IIM Bangalore
description: In this short video, Prof. B Mahadevan addresses all educators who aspire to become great academics and offers them some thumb rules based on his experiences in teaching.

youtubeTitle: Traits of a Confident Teacher by Professor B Mahadevan
author: IIM Bangalore
description: In this video, Prof. B Mahadevan brings to light a question that often crosses educators’ minds, especially the ones at the beginning of their career; the question is if they are capable of teaching with confidence.

sheetTitle: Importance of a Detailed Session Plan
youtubeTitle: Importance of a Detailed Session Plan by Professor B Mahadevan
author: IIM Bangalore
description: Effective classroom delivery is all about a logical story unwinding in the class. Prof. B Mahadevan says a detailed session plan is necessary to achieve this. He goes on to provide educators some useful tips on developing a session plan.

sheetTitle: How Often Should You Start a New Elective
youtubeTitle: How Often Should You Start a New Elective by Professor B Mahadevan
author: IIM Bangalore
description: In his talk, Prof. B Mahadevan shares his thoughts around how often an educator should start a new elective. He states that in a business school, issues unfold faster than imagined and educators must keep pace and come up with more electives.

youtubeTitle: Challenges in Teaching
author: IIM Bangalore
description:
In this short video, Prof. Sourav Mukherji talks about the challenges educators face when teaching. He focuses on two factors – demand side (student perspective) and supply side (teacher perspective).

author: IIM Bangalore
description: Content is no longer the king and educators should redefine their roles. In this video, Prof. Sourav Mukherji stresses on the importance of learner-centric education.

youtubeTitle: Bringing Research into the Classroom
author: IIM Bangalore
description: In this video, Professor Nilam Kaushik delves into the ‘whys’ and ‘hows’ of bringing research into the classroom. When academics transition to becoming knowledge producers from being knowledge consumers, they are in a position to understand (i) why it makes sense for research to be brought into the classroom, (ii) how they can bring research into the classroom, and (iii) what elements can be brought in the classroom for an engaging classroom experience.

youtubeTitle: Integrating Research into Teaching: Professor Varun Jindal, IIM Bangalore
author: IIM Bangalore
description: In this video, Professor Varun Jindal talks about linking one’s research into their teaching. He starts by speaking about the benefits to the educator, and then advances to discussing about the benefits to students. Finally, Prof. Jindal discusses the courses that are more suited for research-informed teaching.

youtubeTitle: Interconnections between Research and Teaching: Professor Jitamitra Desai, IIM Bangalore
author: IIM Bangalore
description: In this video, Professor Jitamitra Desai addresses the interconnections between research and teaching. He focuses on the common tension that exists between the two, explores if they are mutually synergistic, and discusses how an academic institution should prioritize both activities.

sheetTitle: How Generative AI Is Transforming Teaching and Learning
youtubeTitle: How Generative AI Is Transforming Teaching and Learning | Prof.Naveen Kumar Bhansali - 02
author: SANGAM | Digital Learning Community
description:
In this engaging discussion, educators explore how Generative AI (Gen AI) is transforming the world of teaching and learning. From lesson planning to classroom engagement, Gen AI is enabling faculty to create more contextualized, personalized, and domain-specific learning experiences — even when students come from diverse backgrounds and disciplines.

The conversation dives deep into how teachers can:

Use AI tools to generate relevant examples, analogies, and case studies

Adapt content to different student contexts and domains

Maintain authenticity while leveraging AI support

Recognize and manage AI’s limitations — such as bias and “beautiful hallucinations”

Strike the right balance between human expertise and AI assistance

Through humor, reflection, and practical insights, this session sheds light on how educators can responsibly integrate AI into their teaching practices to enhance creativity, inclusivity, and understanding in the classroom.
